newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi promises tough budget fight.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi promises tough budget fight.

text.p: Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi on Thursday unveiled his 1997 "counter-budget" proposal, vowing to lead strong opposition in parliament to the centre-left government's fiscal package.

"With this budget (the government's) we have to have a tough opposition...ours will be strong, true, decisive, determined and certainly never forget the interests of the country," Berlusconi, leader of the centre-right Freedom Alliance, said.

The budget, which was approved by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's cabinet last week and is due to be officially presented to parliament on Thursday, aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's projected deficit.

Among measures included in the budget is a five percent increase in taxes on house and land ownership as well as a five percent increase in the valuations local authorities can base their property taxes on.

Berlusconi, who served as prime minister for seven months in 1994, criticised a proposal in Prodi's budget for a one-off "Euro-tax" to help Italy achieve the three percent deficit-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio required by the Maastricht treaty to qualify for Economic and Monetary Union.
He said the "Euro-tax" would create "a vicious cycle of economic depression".

Berlusconi said his "counter-budget" proposed cutting the deficit by 62.1 trillion lire ($40.9 billion), encompassing 33.1 trillion ($21.8 billion) in spending cuts and 29 trillion ($19.1 billion) in additional revenues.
